response:
This analysis contains 30056 tracts across 20 metro areas on census2023-tract boundaries. Scope: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations..

EPA walkability score (1–20): mean 11.60, across 29,485 tracts; 571 missing.

Estimated park access (%): mean 69.85, across 23,932 tracts; 6,124 missing.

Mapped gathering-place features: mean 3.07, across 30,056 tracts; 0 missing.

Mapped gathering-place features per 1,000 residents: mean 1.17, across 29,722 tracts; 334 missing.

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

definitions.distress_pct: Modeled crude adult frequent mental-distress prevalence (%).
definitions.walkability: Population-mass weighted EPA index on a 1–20 scale, strict support sample.
definitions.walkability_partial: Diagnostic EPA score before excluding incomplete crosswalk support; not the primary exposure.
definitions.epa_population_coverage_pct: Percent of author's modeled ACS2019 block population supported by usable EPA sources.
definitions.pop_density: ACS residents per square kilometer of Census land area.
definitions.park_access_pct: Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
definitions.amenities_per_1000: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
definitions.amenities_count: Count of selected mapped OSM features assigned to the tract.
definitions.park_population_coverage_pct: Percent of 2020 block-point population inside published ParkServe place coverage; missing access values are not zeros.
definitions.park_population_2020: 2020 Census population summed over all populated blocks with this reviewed tract parent ID.
definitions.park_covered_population_2020: 2020 block population whose internal point lies in published ParkServe place coverage.
definitions.park_served_population_2020: 2020 block population whose internal point lies in both published coverage and an open-access park service area.

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.

sources.title: ACS 2019–2023 five-year Detailed Tables, official bulk files
notes: Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.

sources.title: CDC PLACES frequent mental distress, crude prevalence
notes: Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

sources.title: Amos (2021), 2020 Census Block Crosswalk Data, V2
sources.release: V2, CC BY 4.0; 2019 block groups → 2020 blocks
notes: Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.
Outgoing population shares are normalized only within 0.5% rounding tolerance, then multiplied by each EPA block group's 2018 TotPop to form population masses.
2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.
Attribution: Brian Amos (2021), doi:10.7910/DVN/T9VMJO, Harvard Dataverse V2; CC BY 4.0.

sources.title: Trust for Public Land ParkServe public parks and 10-minute walk service areas
notes: Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.
Trust for Public Land attribution and terms: https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/ParkServe_Terms_of_Use_May_2024.pdf

sources.title: OpenStreetMap contributors: mapped gathering-place features
sources.geography: Point/feature centers assigned to Census 2023 tracts
notes: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

coverage_finding.claim: This analysis contains 30056 tracts across 20 metro areas on census2023-tract boundaries. Scope: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations..

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.
Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

GEOID20 is a service field name, not a claim of 2020 geography; source IDs are matched to the author's 2019-block-group crosswalk.

Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.
Outgoing population shares are normalized only within 0.5% rounding tolerance, then multiplied by each EPA block group's 2018 TotPop to form population masses.
2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.

Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.

Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.
Coverage describes the loaded snapshot; it does not independently verify a top-20 metro universe.

result.claim: walkability: mean 11.599 (29485 nonmissing tracts); park_access_pct: mean 69.848 (23932 nonmissing tracts); amenities_count: mean 3.066 (30056 nonmissing tracts); amenities_per_1000: mean 1.170 (29722 nonmissing tracts).
caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.
Index is relative walkability on a 1–20 scale, not measured walking, safety, or social interaction.
GEOID20 is a service field name, not a claim of 2020 geography; source IDs are matched to the author's 2019-block-group crosswalk.

Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.
Trust for Public Land attribution and terms: https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/ParkServe_Terms_of_Use_May_2024.pdf

Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.
Means are unweighted across tracts; percentages use 0–100 units; income is in dollars.

result.question: Summarize walkability, park access, and mapped gathering-place amenities for the full loaded 20-metro study. State units, available tract counts, how park access was derived, and mapping/coverage limits.

findings.claim: This analysis contains 30056 tracts across 20 metro areas on census2023-tract boundaries. Scope: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations..

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.
Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.
Trust for Public Land attribution and terms: https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/ParkServe_Terms_of_Use_May_2024.pdf

Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.
Coverage describes the loaded snapshot; it does not independently verify a top-20 metro universe.

findings.claim: walkability: mean 11.599 (29485 nonmissing tracts); park_access_pct: mean 69.848 (23932 nonmissing tracts); amenities_count: mean 3.066 (30056 nonmissing tracts); amenities_per_1000: mean 1.170 (29722 nonmissing tracts).
caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.
Index is relative walkability on a 1–20 scale, not measured walking, safety, or social interaction.
GEOID20 is a service field name, not a claim of 2020 geography; source IDs are matched to the author's 2019-block-group crosswalk.

Outgoing population shares are normalized only within 0.5% rounding tolerance, then multiplied by each EPA block group's 2018 TotPop to form population masses.
2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.

Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.

Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.
Means are unweighted across tracts; percentages use 0–100 units; income is in dollars.

sources.title: ACS 2019–2023 five-year Detailed Tables, official bulk files
notes: Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.

sources.title: CDC PLACES frequent mental distress, crude prevalence
notes: Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

sources.release: V2, CC BY 4.0; 2019 block groups → 2020 blocks
notes: Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.

2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.

notes: Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap contributors: mapped gathering-place features
sources.geography: Point/feature centers assigned to Census 2023 tracts
notes: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.

response:
This analysis contains 30056 tracts across 20 metro areas on census2023-tract boundaries. Scope: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations..

Modeled frequent mental distress (%): mean 16.01, across 28,665 tracts; 1,391 missing.

Poverty (%): mean 11.94, across 29,672 tracts; 384 missing.

Tract median household income ($): mean 101,340.91, across 29,459 tracts; 597 missing.

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

definitions.distress_pct: Modeled crude adult frequent mental-distress prevalence (%).
definitions.walkability: Population-mass weighted EPA index on a 1–20 scale, strict support sample.
definitions.walkability_partial: Diagnostic EPA score before excluding incomplete crosswalk support; not the primary exposure.
definitions.epa_population_coverage_pct: Percent of author's modeled ACS2019 block population supported by usable EPA sources.
definitions.pop_density: ACS residents per square kilometer of Census land area.
definitions.park_access_pct: Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
definitions.amenities_per_1000: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
definitions.amenities_count: Count of selected mapped OSM features assigned to the tract.
definitions.park_population_coverage_pct: Percent of 2020 block-point population inside published ParkServe place coverage; missing access values are not zeros.
definitions.park_population_2020: 2020 Census population summed over all populated blocks with this reviewed tract parent ID.
definitions.park_covered_population_2020: 2020 block population whose internal point lies in published ParkServe place coverage.
definitions.park_served_population_2020: 2020 block population whose internal point lies in both published coverage and an open-access park service area.

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.

sources.title: CDC PLACES frequent mental distress, crude prevalence
notes: Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

sources.title: Amos (2021), 2020 Census Block Crosswalk Data, V2
sources.release: V2, CC BY 4.0; 2019 block groups → 2020 blocks
notes: Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.
Outgoing population shares are normalized only within 0.5% rounding tolerance, then multiplied by each EPA block group's 2018 TotPop to form population masses.
2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.
Attribution: Brian Amos (2021), doi:10.7910/DVN/T9VMJO, Harvard Dataverse V2; CC BY 4.0.

notes: Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap contributors: mapped gathering-place features
sources.geography: Point/feature centers assigned to Census 2023 tracts
notes: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.
Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.
Outgoing population shares are normalized only within 0.5% rounding tolerance, then multiplied by each EPA block group's 2018 TotPop to form population masses.
2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.

Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.
Trust for Public Land attribution and terms: https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/ParkServe_Terms_of_Use_May_2024.pdf

Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.
Coverage describes the loaded snapshot; it does not independently verify a top-20 metro universe.

Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.
Coverage describes the loaded snapshot; it does not independently verify a top-20 metro universe.

findings.claim: distress_pct: mean 16.011 (28665 nonmissing tracts); poverty_pct: mean 11.943 (29672 nonmissing tracts); income: mean 101340.911 (29459 nonmissing tracts).
caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.
Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

notes: Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.

Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap contributors: mapped gathering-place features
sources.geography: Point/feature centers assigned to Census 2023 tracts
notes: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.

response:
Unadjusted: +0.0563 percentage points of modeled distress per 1-point higher walkability. Based on 28,369 tracts; 1,687 excluded for missing data.

95% interval: -0.0041 to +0.1167 (metro-clustered).

The interval includes zero, so the direction of the association is uncertain.

Adjusted: -0.0659 percentage points of modeled distress per 1-point higher walkability. Based on 28,150 tracts; 1,906 excluded for missing data.

95% interval: -0.1004 to -0.0313 (metro-clustered).

Adjusted interaction: +0.0003 percentage points of modeled distress per 1-point higher walkability, slope change per 10 percentage points of park access. Based on 22,518 tracts; 7,538 excluded for missing data.

95% interval: -0.0064 to +0.0070 (metro-clustered).

The interval includes zero, so the direction of the association is uncertain.

The fitted association changes direction after adjustment. The pattern is sensitive to the included controls; this does not establish a mechanism.

Adjustment includes poverty, income, age, racial/ethnic composition and population density; pooled models also include metro fixed effects.

These are neighborhood associations, not proof that walkability improves an individual's mental health. CDC distress is modeled; loneliness and social connection are not directly measured. Explaining why requires literature evidence and stronger study designs.

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

definitions.distress_pct: Modeled crude adult frequent mental-distress prevalence (%).
definitions.walkability: Population-mass weighted EPA index on a 1–20 scale, strict support sample.
definitions.walkability_partial: Diagnostic EPA score before excluding incomplete crosswalk support; not the primary exposure.
definitions.epa_population_coverage_pct: Percent of author's modeled ACS2019 block population supported by usable EPA sources.
definitions.pop_density: ACS residents per square kilometer of Census land area.
definitions.park_access_pct: Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
definitions.amenities_per_1000: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
definitions.amenities_count: Count of selected mapped OSM features assigned to the tract.
definitions.park_population_coverage_pct: Percent of 2020 block-point population inside published ParkServe place coverage; missing access values are not zeros.
definitions.park_population_2020: 2020 Census population summed over all populated blocks with this reviewed tract parent ID.
definitions.park_covered_population_2020: 2020 block population whose internal point lies in published ParkServe place coverage.
definitions.park_served_population_2020: 2020 block population whose internal point lies in both published coverage and an open-access park service area.

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.

notes: Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

sources.title: Amos (2021), 2020 Census Block Crosswalk Data, V2
sources.release: V2, CC BY 4.0; 2019 block groups → 2020 blocks
notes: Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.
Outgoing population shares are normalized only within 0.5% rounding tolerance, then multiplied by each EPA block group's 2018 TotPop to form population masses.
2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.

Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap contributors: mapped gathering-place features
sources.geography: Point/feature centers assigned to Census 2023 tracts
notes: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

coverage_finding.claim: This analysis contains 30056 tracts across 20 metro areas on census2023-tract boundaries. Scope: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations..

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.
Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.
Outgoing population shares are normalized only within 0.5% rounding tolerance, then multiplied by each EPA block group's 2018 TotPop to form population masses.
2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.

Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.
Trust for Public Land attribution and terms: https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/ParkServe_Terms_of_Use_May_2024.pdf

Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.
Coverage describes the loaded snapshot; it does not independently verify a top-20 metro universe.

evidence.standard_errors: metro-clustered with finite-sample correction and t reference
evidence.weighting: equal weight per complete tract; not person-level

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

response:
This analysis contains 1504 tracts across 1 metro areas on census2023-tract boundaries. Scope: Selected metro: Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell, GA.

Unadjusted: +0.0462 percentage points of modeled distress per 1-point higher walkability. Based on 1,462 tracts; 42 excluded for missing data.

No confidence interval is reported: there are fewer than 10 metro clusters. Treat this as an exploratory description.

Adjusted: -0.0710 percentage points of modeled distress per 1-point higher walkability. Based on 1,449 tracts; 55 excluded for missing data.

No confidence interval is reported: there are fewer than 10 metro clusters. Treat this as an exploratory description.

The fitted association changes direction after adjustment. The pattern is sensitive to the included controls; this does not establish a mechanism.

Adjustment includes poverty, income, age, racial/ethnic composition and population density; pooled models also include metro fixed effects.

These are neighborhood associations, not proof that walkability improves an individual's mental health. CDC distress is modeled; loneliness and social connection are not directly measured. Explaining why requires literature evidence and stronger study designs.

Still unanswered: No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded. Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.

scope.description: Twenty largest US metropolitan statistical areas by Census Vintage 2023 population; full constituent counties, July 2023 OMB delineations.

definitions.distress_pct: Modeled crude adult frequent mental-distress prevalence (%).
definitions.walkability: Population-mass weighted EPA index on a 1–20 scale, strict support sample.
definitions.walkability_partial: Diagnostic EPA score before excluding incomplete crosswalk support; not the primary exposure.
definitions.epa_population_coverage_pct: Percent of author's modeled ACS2019 block population supported by usable EPA sources.
definitions.pop_density: ACS residents per square kilometer of Census land area.
definitions.park_access_pct: Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
definitions.amenities_per_1000: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
definitions.amenities_count: Count of selected mapped OSM features assigned to the tract.
definitions.park_population_coverage_pct: Percent of 2020 block-point population inside published ParkServe place coverage; missing access values are not zeros.
definitions.park_population_2020: 2020 Census population summed over all populated blocks with this reviewed tract parent ID.
definitions.park_covered_population_2020: 2020 block population whose internal point lies in published ParkServe place coverage.
definitions.park_served_population_2020: 2020 block population whose internal point lies in both published coverage and an open-access park service area.

caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap contributors: mapped gathering-place features
sources.geography: Point/feature centers assigned to Census 2023 tracts
notes: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.

coverage_finding.claim: This analysis contains 1504 tracts across 1 metro areas on census2023-tract boundaries. Scope: Selected metro: Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell, GA.
caveats: Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
The study combines older built-environment measures, interpolated population weights, ACS period estimates, and modeled 2023 health outcomes.
Crosswalk review is documented and checked in code, not an independent validation of interpolated weights.
Minor boundary/cartographic changes can remain even when 2020 and 2023 tract ID inventories agree.

CDC PLACES 2025 omits Pennsylvania's 2023 frequent-mental-distress estimates. Philadelphia health/model samples cover only available non-Pennsylvania portions, not the full metro. Do not generalize those subset results to the whole metro. See https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/ .
No tract adjacency file is included; residual Moran diagnostics are unavailable, while metro clustering remains available.
Missing observations remain missing; the analyst must disclose complete-case exclusions.
No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Park access uses 2020 block population points and retrieved ParkServe polygons; OSM is a later mapped inventory. Neither measures actual use or social interaction.
Official bulk cells match the keyed Census API; no API key is used for these downloads.
Period estimates for 2019–2023; selected raw 90% margins of error retained, not propagated.

Fourteen Suffolk County NY tract rows are unpublished; Census collection-error suppression is documented at https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/errata/148.html . These rows remain missing.
Poverty uses the population for whom poverty status is determined; Black alone and Hispanic of any race overlap.
Modeled estimates, not direct tract observations; BRFSS/ACS/census inputs.

The 2025 release omits Pennsylvania and Kentucky estimates for 2023-BRFSS-based measures. Pennsylvania's omission leaves the Philadelphia metro partially observed; no older-release values are substituted. https://www.cdc.gov/places/current-release-notes/
Frequent mental distress: at least 14 mentally unhealthy days in the previous 30 days, adults 18+.
Does not directly measure loneliness or social connection, and cannot evaluate intervention effects.

Crosswalk uses 2010 population and NLCD2016-informed interpolation within split blocks; it is an estimate, not observed 2023 population movement.
Outgoing population shares are normalized only within 0.5% rounding tolerance, then multiplied by each EPA block group's 2018 TotPop to form population masses.
2020 block parent tract IDs are validated against both 2020 and 2023 tract inventories; this is not proof of exact polygon equality.
Main walkability additionally excludes targets with more than 1% land-area change between 2020 and 2023 or an undefined area comparison. This is a study QC rule, not a validated accuracy threshold.
Main walkability excludes tracts with unsupported positive-population blocks in the author's reallocated ACS2019 reference population. Partial scores are retained separately.

Estimated percent of 2020 Census population whose block internal point falls in a published ParkServe 10-minute walk service area for an open-access park. Only tracts with all populated block points inside the published ParkServe place coverage and passing the existing boundary review are reported. This is a study-derived block-point approximation, not TPL's official statistic.
ParkServe coverage is uneven outside its published urban places; incomplete population support remains missing.
Block internal points approximate where residents live; access points and street networks have errors. Park access does not measure use, quality, safety, or social contact.
Strict coverage selects a more urban/municipal subset; park-access analyses do not represent every tract in the metro.
Service metadata includes legacy date labels; retrieval date is not an assertion that all parks were updated in that year.
Trust for Public Land attribution and terms: https://parkserve.tpl.org/downloads/ParkServe_Terms_of_Use_May_2024.pdf

sources.title: OpenStreetMap contributors: mapped gathering-place features
sources.geography: Point/feature centers assigned to Census 2023 tracts
notes: Mapped OSM gathering-place features per 1,000 ACS residents: cafe, pub, library, community_centre, social_centre, place_of_worship, marketplace. Nodes use their coordinates; ways/relations use their bounding-box centers. Explicit private, no-access and members-only features are excluded. Counts are mapped features, not verified unique venues.
© OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL). Counted once per OSM type/ID; multiple mapped features can represent one venue.
Zero means no matching mapped feature, not no real venue. Volunteer mapping completeness varies and commercial venues may require spending.
Feature centers can fall outside the feature or on the other side of a tract boundary. Current mapped venues are temporally mismatched with older health and ACS estimates.

gaps: No direct loneliness or social-connection measures are loaded.
Cross-sectional tract associations cannot establish causation or individual effects.
